summary: The root مزج (mzj) refers to mixing or mingling. It can describe an admixture, what is mixed with a drink, or the constitution/temperament of the body (its humors).
lane: مِزْجُ شَىْءٍ ذ , and , What is mixed, or mingled, with a thing; its admixture. (TA.) -b2- الشَّرَابِ What is mixed with mine, or a beverage. (S, K.) الخَمْرِ كَافُورٌ [see Kur, lxxvi., 5,] The odour, not the taste, of the wine is [ like ] camphor. (TA.) -b3- البَدَنِ [ The constitution, or temperament, of the body; ] the aggregate natural constituents ( طَبَائِعُ ) with which the body is composed; (S, K;) i. e. the four humours of the body; namely, black bile [ السَّوْدَآءُ ], yellow bile [ الصَّفْرَآءُ ], ( المِرَّتَانِ ), phlegm ( البَلْغَمُ ), and blood ( الدَّمُ ). (TA) Pl. أَمْزِجَةٌ . (Msb.) You say, هُوَ صَحِيحُ , and فَاسِدُهُ , He is of sound, and of unsound, constitution, or temperament: meaning the humours of the body. And أَمْزِجَةُ النِّسَآءِ مُخْتَلِفَةٌ The constitutions, or temperaments, of women are discordant, or various. (A.) -b4- مِزْجٌ (As, K, &c.) and , (Az, S, &c.,) or the latter is erroneous, or a word of weak authority, (K,) Honey: (S, K:) or honey in the comb; syn. شَهْدٌ : (T:) so called because every sweet beverage is mixed with it. (AHn.) -b5- Also, Water with which wine is mixed. (TA.) -b6- مِزْجٌ The bitter almond; as also : see لَوْزٌ (K:) but IDrd doubts of its correctness; and it is said to be correctly مُنْج [which is Persian]. (TA.)

headwords.def: (S, K,) aor. مَزُجَ, (L Msb,) [not مَزَجَ, as in the lexicons of Golius and Freytag,] inf. n. مَزْجٌ, (K, &c.,) He mixed, mingled, incorporated, or blended, (S, K,) a thing with ( بِ ) water; (Msb;) or beverage, or wine, ( شَرَاب,) with something else. (S.) مَزَجَ (tropical:) He exasperated, or irritated. (K.) مَزَجْتُهُ عَلَى صَاحِبِهِ I enraged him, and exasperated him, or irritated him, against his companion. (A.)

inf. n. تَمْزِيجٌ, He gave. (K.) Ex. مزّج السَّائِلَ He gave the beggar something. (ISh.) مزّج, inf. n. تَمْزِيجٌ, It (an ear of corn, K, and a grape, TA,) became changed in colour from green to yellow. (T, K.)

inf. n. مُمَازَجَةٌ, It mixed, mingled, commingled, intermixed, intermingled, or became incorporated or blended, with it; as some does with water. (TA.) مازجهُ, (tropical:) He contended with him, or disputed with him, for glory, or honour, or glorious or honourable qualities, and the like. (K.)
and They two mixed, or mingled, or became mixed or mingled, each with the other. (TA.)
It was, or became, mixed with ( بِ ) another thing. (TA.) See 6.
شَرَابٌ مَزْجٌ i. q., Mixed mine, or beverage. (TA.) See مِزْجٌ.

مِزْجُ شَىْءٍ , and, What is mixed, or mingled, with a thing; its admixture. (TA.) الشَّرَابِ What is mixed with mine, or a beverage. (S, K.) الخَمْرِ كَافُورٌ [see Kur, lxxvi., 5,] The odour, not the taste, of the wine is [ like ] camphor. (TA.) البَدَنِ [ The constitution, or temperament, of the body; ] the aggregate natural constituents ( طَبَائِعُ ) with which the body is composed; (S, K;) i. e.
A boot, (K,) worn by women: (A:) an arabicized word, (S, K,) from the Persian مُوزَهْ: (S:) pl. مَوَازِجَةٌ (because it is a foreign word, S) and مَوَازِجُ. (S, K.)
رَجُلٌ مَزَّاجٌ , and; A man who continues not of one disposition, or temper, but varies in disposition, or temper: or a liar, who confounds, or confuses, things. (IAar.)
طَبْعُ عُطَارِدَ مُتَمَزِّجٌ [ The nature of the planet Mercury is various ]. (A.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
